text: Oh... and you said it was fake. 😢
So should we go or not, dear?
Oops. Kuya Jun says it is real. What now?
"Sorry, Tita! I should have checked before I said that. Thank you for sharing it. Lola, let us go on Wednesday."
Sorry Tita! I should have checked before I said that. Thank you for sharing it. Lola, let us go on Wednesday.
A quick, honest sorry and a fix. Tita forgives you.
Check the page together and thank Kuya Jun
Let me check the page together with Kuya Jun, and thank you, Tita.
You checked, and you thanked both of them.
"Anyone can fake a page name. I still do not trust it."
Anyone can fake a page name. I still do not trust it.
Kuya Jun is a real person who runs it. Doubting everything is as unhelpful as trusting everything.
Wednesday is on!
You checked, said "this one is legit", and shared it. Lola brings her grandchild for her shots, and three moms from the Barangay Moms group say they will come too.
Thank you, dear! We will bring the vaccine card.
See you all on Wednesday morning! 😊
Family's Light! You know when to trust, too.
A little late, still good
The good news got through, but someone felt dismissed, or only a few families heard about it. Checking and saying "this is legit" works best when it is early and warm.
Lola, bring the vaccine card on Wednesday. We will see you!
Okay! 🙏
So close! Trusting the right thing is a skill too.
The free day is missed
Doubts lingered, and Lola decided to wait. The free vaccination day passed. Kuya Jun will hold another one, and Lola will go next week.
No worries, Lola. We have another Wednesday next week.
Oops, I should have checked first. 😅
Doubting everything is a trap too, friend. Check, then trust what checks out. Try again?
ARAW: AI Relevance Activities and Workshops
User Guide
ARAW teaches you when to trust AI and health information, one short game at a time. This guide shows each screen with numbered pictures. Read it from the top, or jump to the part you need.

ARAW quick start
Learn when to trust AI and health info.
Open ARAW
Open the ARAW link or icon. Pick English, press SELECT, then press START.
Tap Learn, then the module where Ara stands. Read each card and tap an answer.
"So close!" means read the tip and try another answer. No one loses for trying.
Read the post. Press FACT or FAKE. Read why. Every fake gets a FAKE stamp.
Tap Arcade for short games. Tap, click, or use the arrow keys.
Make it easier
Tap Me. Turn on Larger text or Extra-large buttons. Turn the music off if you like.
Ask
When should I trust it? For health worries, always ask your health worker.
Need help? Press the flag (Report) on any screen.
Getting started
ARAW works in the web browser of any phone, tablet or computer. You do not need an account.
The very first screen asks for your language. Tap a language card, then press SELECT. ARAW is in English for now; more languages are coming.
The ARAW language screen: the title box with the English card picked, the gold SELECT button under it, and Ara in front of a pixel sunrise sky.
Tap your language. The picked card turns blue and its little box fills in.
Press SELECT. The music starts and the sun begins to rise.
You can change the language later in Me, under Settings.
Wait for the sunrise, then press START
Next, the sun rises behind Ara and the loading bar fills. When the bar is full, press START.
The ARAW start screen: the title box at the top, Ara in front of a pixel sunrise, and a big gold START button at the bottom.
The name of the app and what it is for.
Sound switches. Turn music or sound effects on or off before you start.
Press START to go to the Home screen.
Turn sound on or off
ARAW has soft music and small sound effects. You can turn each one off at any time. Your choice is saved on this device.
On the start screen, use the Music and Sound effects switches.
Later, open Me and scroll to Sound to change them again.
In a quiet room or a group session, turn the music off and keep the effects low.
Install ARAW on your phone
You can add ARAW to your home screen like an app. After the first visit it also works without internet.
Android (Chrome): tap the three dots at the top right, then "Add to Home screen" or "Install app".
iPhone (Safari): tap the Share button, then "Add to Home Screen".
Computer (Chrome or Edge): click the install icon at the right end of the address bar.
Open ARAW from the new icon. It opens full screen.
Your progress stays on this device only. If you clear the browser data, your progress is cleared too.
The Home screen
Home shows what to do next. Use the buttons at the bottom (on a phone) or on the left (on a computer) to move around.
See your next lesson
Ara greets you and shows the next lesson. Press CONTINUE to keep learning where you stopped.
The Home screen on a phone: XP and streak chips at the top, Ara saying good morning, a Continue card for Module 5, and the tab bar at the bottom.
Your points (XP) and your streak: how many days in a row you have played.
How much of this lesson you have done.
Continue the lesson.
Report a problem from any screen.
Go to Home, Learn, Arcade, Library or Me.
More on Home
Scroll down for the Daily Challenge, a myth of the day and the Arcade.
Lower part of Home: the Daily Challenge card, the Myth of the day card, and the Arcade card.
Today's challenge: one game and three quick questions.
Myth of the day. Tap the card to flip it and read the fact.
A shortcut to the games.
Learn: lessons step by step
There are ten short modules. Each takes about 12 to 15 minutes and ends with the same question: when should I trust it?
Modules open one after another. A check mark means done. A lock means you finish the one before it first.
The Learn path: four finished modules with check marks, module 5 lit up with Ara above it, and locked modules below.
A finished module. You can replay it any time.
Your next module. Ara stands on it.
A locked module. Finish the one before it to open it.
How many modules you have finished.
Open a module
Tap a module to see what it teaches, how long it takes and the badge you can earn. Then press START or CONTINUE.
Details of Module 5, Check Before You Share: the game, the time, what you will learn, the badge, and a Continue button.
The module name and what you will learn.
Start or continue the module.
Answer a lesson card
Read the card and tap an answer. If it is not right, ARAW says "So close!" and explains why. Then try another answer. No one loses points for trying.
A lesson card asking what a computer learned from 1,000 mango photos. The wrong answer is marked, a So close! note explains why, and Ara reacts.
Close the lesson. Your place is saved.
How far you are in this module.
Ara reacts to your answer and gives a hint.
The answer you picked.
"So close!" tells you why, so you can try again.
NEXT opens when the card is done.
On a computer you can press the number keys to pick an answer, and Enter for NEXT.
Rewards and badges
Each finished module gives you XP and a badge. Ara celebrates with you. See all your badges in Me, in the Badge cabinet.
The Badge cabinet on the Me screen, with earned badges in colour and locked ones in grey.
Tap a badge to see how to earn it.
Fact or Fake and the Truth Radar
Fact or Fake shows ten posts, messages or pictures. You decide: is it fact or fake? Every fake is made up for the game and gets a FAKE stamp.
Decide: fact or fake?
Read the post. Then press FACT or FAKE. On a phone you can also swipe: right for fact, left for fake.
A Fact or Fake item: a made-up social media post, with a red FAKE button and a green FACT button below it.
Which item you are on, out of ten.
The post to check. Read it slowly.
Press FAKE if you think it is false.
Press FACT if you think it is true.
Keyboard: right arrow or L for Fact, left arrow or A for Fake.
Read the feedback
After each answer, a card tells you if you were right, why, and how to check it in real life.
The same post with a red ARAW GAME FAKE stamp, and a green card that says Correct! It is FAKE, with the reason and how to check.
The FAKE stamp shows the post was made up for the game.
Why it is fact or fake, and how to check.
Report this item if something looks wrong.
Go to the next item.
At the end you see your score and your Truth Radar. The radar shows whether you lean too trusting, too doubtful, or balanced. Balanced is the goal.
The results screen: the score out of ten, the Truth Radar meter with a pin, a short verdict and a Play again button.
How many you got right, and the XP you earned.
The Truth Radar: how well you tell fact from fake.
Do you lean trusting, doubtful, or balanced? A tip follows.
Play another round with new items.
Arcade games
The Arcade has short games about AI and health. Every run is different. Games open as you finish modules.
Pick a game
The top card shows today's featured game. Below are all the games. Tap one to see what it is about.
The Arcade: a featured game card with a Play button at the top, and game tiles below with their best scores.
Today's featured game. Everyone plays the same run today.
A game tile with its topic and your best score.
Play Fact or Fake from the Arcade
Scroll down in the Arcade to play Fact or Fake as often as you like.
